targetSets.name: lifecycle-transition-tables
targetSets.description: AB-92 AC1/AC2's armorer ExecutionHandle transition guards: the state checks that decide whether an execution may move from one ExecutionState to another. An unasserted branch here would let a caller drive an impossible transition (e.g. aborting an already-terminal execution) with no test catching it.

targets.why: Gates every ExecutionState transition abort() is allowed to cause: refuses from terminal/unknown-effect/cleanup-pending, refuses a second abort-requested, otherwise transitions to abort-requested and forwards the AbortController signal. occurrence 1 selects the per-execution closure (line ~335) over the file's unrelated bulk abort(selector, ...) method (line ~482), which shares the name but fans out to the per-execution one rather than gating a transition itself.

targetSets.name: cancellation-propagation
targetSets.description: AB-92 AC3's Bureau-level cancellation boundary: Bureau.abortRun's fan-out from the public API call into the owned ActiveRun's own abort(), the one path AB-268's contract matrix drives through its 'targeted-abort' and 'root-subtree-abort' scenarios.

targets.why: Idempotency guard (repeat call or already-settled run returns the current summary instead of re-aborting) plus the once-only abortingRunIds admission that actually calls activeRun.abort().

equivalentMutants.reason: abortingRunIds.delete(id) in the early terminal-status branch (AB-353, PR #570 review — pinned to this exact line rather than matched by operator alone, so a later, genuinely non-equivalent remove-statement survivor at a different line in this same target is never silently misattributed). abortingRunIds.has(id) is read in exactly one place, guarded behind the earlier `if (runState.status !== 'running') return ...` branch: once a run leaves 'running' for any reason, every future abortRun(id) call is intercepted there before ever consulting the set again, so whether a given id was ever deleted from abortingRunIds cannot change any future call's behavior. Run ids are never reused (AB-337's identifier seam), so a leaked entry cannot collide with a later run either. No public API enumerates, sizes, or inspects this set (confirmed by grep: `abortingRunIds` has no reader outside abortRun itself), so it fails the AB-92 AC4 ResourceScope/QuiescenceReport discovery test for a 'leaked resource' too — the only way to observe the difference is reaching into private module state, which this project's own test-helper-parity rule (`documentation/operative-type-safe-api.md:822-824`) already rules out as a legitimate test technique.

The detachBestEffortPromise(...closed().then(...)) statement wrapping the closed()-continuation delete (AB-353). Same reasoning as line 4478: this statement's only effect is eventually clearing an entry from abortingRunIds, which the earlier status guard makes unreachable to read again regardless of whether it was ever cleared. See line 4478's entry for the full argument, including why abortingRunIds.add(id) itself is deliberately NOT covered by an equivalent-mutant entry — it is killed by create-bureau.test.ts's 'abortRun called twice synchronously while still running revokes a pending signed tool-approval review exactly once (AB-353)'.

abortingRunIds.delete(id) inside the closed().then() continuation (AB-353) — the same statement line 4489's wrapper covers when the deletion is REACHED; this entry additionally pins the deletion's own line, since `remove-statement` also produces a candidate for the bare inner ExpressionStatement independent of its enclosing call. See line 4478's entry for the full argument.

tests.testNamePattern: abortRun|aborts a running run|deleteSession aborts every run

targetSets.name: terminal-event-uniqueness
targetSets.description: AB-92 AC1's ActiveRunLiveness terminal-once guards (AB-214 review PRRT_kwDORvupsc6esZSx): status must reach 'terminal' exactly once, and settle() must attach its result and flip status atomically. A survived mutant here means a caller could observe a second terminal snapshot or a result overwritten after settlement with nothing failing.

targets.why: The only place LivenessLifecycleStatus advances; its own-status-unchanged short-circuit and its terminal-once guard are both load-bearing for 'no event after an acknowledged cleanup' (AB-268's structural invariant).

Atomically attaches the terminal result and flips status in one revision; its terminal-once guard is the one thing standing between a single terminal snapshot and a caller observing settle() overwrite an already-settled result.

targetSets.name: cleanup-ownership-resolution
targetSets.description: AB-92 AC3's armorer cleanup-acknowledgement boundary: finish() decides whether an execution's cleanup resolved (state: 'terminal') or is left unresolved for its owner to reconcile (state: 'unknown-effect'), which is the one branch ResourceScope.assertQuiescent() (AB-92 AC4) depends on to tell a leaked resource from an acknowledged one.

targets.why: Chooses 'unknown-effect' vs 'terminal' from the reported CleanupOutcome, retains the privileged context only on a genuinely terminal transition, and resolves the settled promise exactly once (terminal-state short-circuit at the top).
